data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Unlike pure custom builds which often monopolize storage, this proposal hybrids with existing DBs to reduce maintenance.","Active learning loops have stricter latency constraints than general mechanist modeling."],"overturn_conditions":["If an existing tool provides a native, low-latency hook for parameter modification that matches the research schema exactly.","If the team's definition of 'active learning' does not require real-time intervention."],"shared_structure":["Distinction between passive observation and active control.","Necessity of custom infrastructure when external abstractions leak into the control loop.","Separation of transient logic from durable storage to manage risk."],"source_memory_refs":["b1642d037422b51c0be00c872d50beb7dbcd5a47b2733f33a65b653bf158ecb0","f0a7fdb1573a11c5f3064989fd549eaaaafda316476c85270e892ed4058bef0b"],"transfer_claims":["The 'Control Theory Boundary' applies: if the tool must close the loop, it must own the loop's timing and schema.","Hybrid architectures (custom logic + standard storage) mitigate the 'departure' costs usually associated with building from scratch."]},"claim":"A small team should adopt an existing experiment tracker only if their workflow is strictly observational; however, if the research involves active learning loops where the tracker must function as a real-time controller to modify experimental parameters, they must build a custom minimal state machine to avoid the 'integration tax' of hacking rigid external APIs, while mitigating the 'single point of failure' risk by designing the custom tracker as a stateless orchestrator that delegates persistence to a robust, off-the-shelf database.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The team lacks the engineering bandwidth to maintain even a minimal state machine wrapper.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The active learning loop operates on timescales (e.g., days per iteration) where API latency of existing tools is negligible.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The existing tool offers a plugin architecture that allows native injection of control logic without 'hacking'.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Causal Control Boundary: The decision hinges on whether the tracker acts as a passive log (observational) or an active actuator (control). In active loops, latency and schema rigidity in external tools break the causal chain of the experiment. A custom state machine restores this causality by embedding the control logic directly, but to prevent the 'migration cliff' and 'single point of failure,' the custom component handles only transient state transitions, writing immutable event logs to a standard SQL/NoSQL backend immediately, thus separating the fragile control logic from durable storage.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
